statusText: The CME weekend halt still governs this assessment: nothing has quoted NQ since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and nothing will until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about nine hours past the end of this 24-hour horizon. Tail therefore holds at 10% (low), the action stays EA_ON and the status stays green - a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting, and the low non-zero level prices weekend headline discontinuity rather than observed extension. What this hour adds is that the Lebanon front hardened at state level rather than only in militia rhetoric. The toll from the overnight Israeli strikes was revised up to at least 11 killed and 19 wounded, including three children in Ansar; Hezbollah issued a second and sharper statement calling the strikes an escalation driven by Netanyahu's domestic political interests; and Prime Minister Nawaf Salam called the escalation "extremely dangerous" while President Joseph Aoun condemned it as a violation of the June framework agreement. The negotiating track Hezbollah wants abandoned is now under pressure from the Lebanese government side too. Alongside that, ADNOC's cumulative count reached 15 vessels attacked in the strait since February and Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain have all formally condemned Iran, so the Gulf diplomatic front is widening rather than narrowing. Stress therefore rises one point to 55% (elevated). The counterweight is unchanged and equally observed - VIX closed Friday at 14.25, less than a point above its 52-week low of 13.38, and the Nasdaq-100 closed down only 0.13% and about 2.3% below its 52-week high. Confidence is 62% (solid): NQ futures, the NDX cash close, VIX, WTI and Brent, both key Treasury maturities and the full seven-day calendar were each re-read directly this hour, the FOMC minutes date was independently confirmed against Federal Reserve sources, and the price evidence is stale by necessity rather than by omission.
recommendation: Action is EA_ON with a green status, derived from current Tail (10%) alone. No venue quotes NQ anywhere in the 24-hour horizon and no scheduled U.S. macro release falls inside it, so there is no basis for a directional or event-driven block in this window; existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. The operative checkpoint sits just beyond the horizon at the CME reopen near 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, and the danger window brackets that reopen together with its first 90 minutes of price discovery - a full weekend of accumulated headlines expresses there as an opening gap, not as intraday structure. Gap risk remains genuinely two-way. Pulling one way: a Lebanon escalation that now carries explicit Hezbollah retaliation language plus formal condemnation from Lebanon's prime minister and president, a U.S. economic-isolation package explicitly promised for next week, a presidential claim of sovereignty over the strait that Tehran has publicly rejected as impossible to seize "by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier", Iran-Oman reopening talks still unresolved, 15 ADNOC vessels struck in the strait since February with the latest hit on Saturday, WTI at $82.40 after a +5% week and +33% year with an IEA deficit warning attached, and a 10Y at 4.696% pressing a 19-month high. Pulling the other: VIX within a point of its 52-week low, an index that closed the week only 0.13% lower after a third consecutive higher week, and a Friday tape that absorbed the escalation with a mid-range settle rather than a liquidation. Treat the reopen as a checkpoint to be scored on observed price path, not as a pre-committed direction. The dated calendar checkpoints begin Monday and culminate in the FOMC minutes on Wednesday; the undated one - the Treasury's Iran package - is deliberately absent from the verified calendar because no exact date has been published.
headline: Lebanon toll revised to 11 as Hezbollah sharpens its warning and Beirut's president and prime minister condemn the strikes, lifting Stress to 55%; with CME shut a second day Tail holds at 10% and the action stays EA_ON.
body:
PRICE PATH (observed, stale by necessity). No venue has quoted NQ since the CME weekly close at 21:00 UTC on Friday 14 August, and none will until the Sunday reopen near 22:00 UTC on 16 August. The last live structure, re-verified this hour from the primary quote page, remains benign: September E-mini Nasdaq-100 futures show a last print of 30,141.75, -46.75 points or -0.15% against a previous close of 30,188.50, on 397,964 contracts, with the session settling inside a 30,028.50-30,283.00 band roughly 255 points or 0.84% wide and no close pinned to either extreme. NQ sits about 2.7% below its 52-week high of 30,975.50 against a 52-week low of 22,961.50. The Nasdaq-100 cash index, re-read directly this hour, closed at 30,046.14, -38.36 points or -0.13%, inside a 29,934.66-30,179.82 range and about 2.3% below its 52-week high of 30,762.20; the week was the third consecutive higher one. A two-way intraday range with a mid-range settle, several percent off the highs, is the opposite of the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension and pinning near extremes that the Tail definition requires. Directional efficiency here is not merely low - it is unmeasurable, because nothing has traded for more than seventeen hours.

CROSS-ASSET (observed, Friday close, all re-verified this hour). The split in the evidence remains the central fact of this assessment. Equity volatility is calm to the point of complacency: VIX closed at 14.25, -0.38 or -2.60% on the day, inside a 14.18-14.72 range and only 0.87 points above its 52-week low of 13.38 against a 52-week high of 35.30. Rates and energy say the opposite. The 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday at 4.696%, +5.5bp on the day and at the top of a 4.625-4.700% range, pressing the 52-week high of 4.747% set earlier in the week; the 2-year closed at 4.171%, +3.1bp, inside a 4.098-4.178% range against a 52-week range of 3.365-4.370%. The curve is therefore steepening on long-end inflation aversion rather than signalling a growth scare. WTI stands at $82.40, +$1.15 or +1.42% on the day, +5% on the week, +3.52% on the month and +32.95% on the year; Brent at $88.52, +$1.45 or +1.67%, +34.43% on the year. Trading Economics attributes the move to the U.S. Treasury's unprecedented economic measures against Iran, the continuing naval blockade of Iranian ports, Houthi strikes on Saudi infrastructure and an IEA warning of the widest 2026 global deficit in five years, partly offset by some Middle Eastern crude reaching U.S. markets. An index within 2.3% of its high while oil is up a third on the year and the long end presses a 19-month high is a conflicted configuration, and by the risk definition a conflict of that kind belongs in Stress, not in Tail.

GEOPOLITICS (new this hour). The Lebanon thread hardened from rhetoric into state-level politics. The toll from the overnight Israeli strikes on Ansar, Nabatieh and Deir ez-Zahrani was revised up to at least 11 killed and 19 wounded, including three children, the deadliest Israeli action in Lebanon since the June framework reduced hostilities, and the strikes reached deeper into the south than any previous post-ceasefire attack. Hezbollah followed its earlier "appropriate response" warning with a second statement naming Netanyahu directly and framing the escalation as serving his domestic political interests. Critically, the Lebanese state aligned against the strikes rather than absorbing them: Prime Minister Nawaf Salam rejected the Israeli justification, called the escalation "extremely dangerous" and reasserted that only the Lebanese state holds authority over military infrastructure, while President Joseph Aoun condemned the strikes as violations of the June framework and of international law. That matters because the direct-negotiation track Hezbollah has demanded be abandoned is now under pressure from both flanks at once. In the strait, ADNOC's cumulative count reached 15 vessels attacked since the war began in February, with the UAE blaming the IRGC for a further strike on Saturday, and Qatar, Kuwait, Egypt and Bahrain have all issued formal condemnations - the Gulf diplomatic front is widening. Iran's deputy foreign minister answered the U.S. president's rally claim that he would declare the strait American territory by saying it "cannot be seized by tweet, nor by aircraft carrier", and Iran's UN ambassador restated that the waterway "will be opened and closed only at Iran's command". Iran-Oman talks on reopening the strait remain unresolved. Vice President Vance framed U.S. objectives as keeping oil and gas cheap and preventing an Iranian weapon, which is the clearest signal yet that the energy channel is the administration's own constraint.

SCORING. Tail stays at 10%. Every ingredient the definition demands - persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements, price holding near extremes - requires a live tape, and there is none; the last observed tape showed the opposite. The 10% is not a claim about structure but a price for weekend headline discontinuity expressing as a Sunday gap. Stress rises one point to 55% (elevated), reflecting a Lebanon escalation that has now drawn formal condemnation from Lebanon's own head of state and head of government, a second and sharper Hezbollah warning, a quantified and still-growing tally of vessel attacks, widening Gulf condemnation, and a U.S. economic-isolation package still promised inside the coming week - against the genuine counterweight of a VIX near its 52-week low and an index that closed the week almost unchanged. Confidence is 62% (solid): coverage this hour was complete across price, volatility, both key rate maturities, both crude benchmarks, the cash index and the seven-day calendar, with the FOMC minutes date independently confirmed against Federal Reserve sources; the only defect is the unavoidable staleness of the price evidence, and two live-blog fetches that were refused were replaced by other primary sources rather than left as gaps. Dominant mode is mixed: complacent equity volatility against stressed rates and energy is precisely a mixed regime, not a trend.

lookbackSummary: Across the trailing 24 clock-hours Tail never left the low band, running 2-10% throughout, so the action was EA_ON and the status green in every available slot. Tail held 7-9% across Friday's U.S. cash session, where the data landed and produced two-way volatility and rotation rather than directional efficiency, then printed 6% into the 21:00 UTC weekly close. Stress traced a clear event arc: 40-44% across Friday afternoon and the U.S. cash session, then easing to 34% at the close. The two runs immediately after the close scored the halt itself at Tail 2% and Stress 12%; from 00:00 UTC onward that reading was corrected back to Tail 9% and Stress 45% on the judgement that a shut venue does not neutralise a live Hormuz closure, and 45% then held for six consecutive hours through 05:00 UTC. From 06:00 UTC the weekend escalation sequence lifted the series steadily - Tail to 10% and Stress through 48%, 50%, 51%, 52%, 53% and 54% - as the Mokha barrage, the Lebanon strikes, the ADNOC vessel attack, the U.S. territorial claim and then Hezbollah's explicit retaliation warning landed one after another with no tape to absorb them. Confidence ran 37-61%, weakest in the hours immediately around the weekly close and settling at 57-61% across the weekend halt as each dimension was re-verified hour by hour. The 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August is unavailable because no successful Claude snapshot was published for that hour; those fields are null and no past opinion has been rewritten.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt - it runs from 14:00 UTC on Saturday 15 August to 13:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, ending roughly nine hours before the reopen near 22:00 UTC that day - so neither a scheduled U.S. macro release nor a tradable price path falls within it. Tail is projected flat at 10% through the remaining Saturday afternoon and evening slots, ticking to 11% from 20:00 UTC as the reopen edges into view and to 12% across the Sunday slots; those increments reflect accumulating gap risk, not observed structure, and every slot stays deep in the low band, so the action is EA_ON and the status green throughout. Stress is projected to hold at 55% through the thin Saturday hours when weekend headline flow is historically lightest, firm to 56% from 20:00 UTC and to 57% from Sunday morning as the unresolved threads converge on the reopen. Confidence drifts from 62% to 56% across the horizon as the last live prints age further without replacement. The material catalyst sits just beyond the horizon: the CME reopen and its first 90 minutes of price discovery, which the danger window brackets. Inside the horizon the realistic risks are headline-driven - an actual Hezbollah retaliation following this hour's hardened warning, a rupture in the Israel-Lebanon negotiating track now that Beirut's president and prime minister have both condemned the strikes, a further Hormuz vessel strike after the sixteenth, an Iranian response to the U.S. territorial claim, an early leak of the promised economic-isolation package, or a breakthrough in the stalled Iran-Oman reopening talks - each of which would move Stress and the expected gap rather than produce observable one-way structure. The first scheduled checkpoint is Monday's Empire State print at 12:30 UTC; the week's highest-impact dated items are Tuesday's housing and industrial production data, the FOMC minutes at 18:00 UTC on Wednesday 19 August, Thursday's claims and Philadelphia Fed pair, and Friday's S&P Global flash PMIs. Its highest-impact undated item is the Treasury's Iran package, omitted from the calendar because no exact date has been published. Nvidia's results on 26 August and the Jackson Hole symposium later that month both fall outside this seven-day window.
